Page03

Brand story

Nonstop
creativity

إبداع ما يوقف

A creative studio built into a van. The truck stops at your door; the creativity doesn't.

Look at the A and the I. A thin road is cut through the A and runs to an orange dot set into the I. That dot is the stop: the moment the truck parks at your door. Read it again and it is a circuit: a line into a node, the way artificial intelligence (AI) is drawn. One mark, both halves of the name.

Slogan: Nonstop creativity · إبداع ما يوقف (set by Amer, 13 October 2026). Sentence case in English, with the orange full stop when it is the headline. The van keeps its descriptor line: Design · AI · Creative services.

Why it works with the logo: the orange dot is the Stop, where the truck parks. The truck stops; the creativity doesn't.

How to write the name: AI Truck. Never Ai Truck, A.I. Truck, AITruck or AI-Truck, and never all capitals in running text (capitals live in the logo only). Inside Arabic text the name stays in Latin letters; spoken, it is إيه آي تراك. to confirm

Brand FixLogo clean-up, colours, fonts and templates your team can use the same afternoon.
Social FixProfiles, grid, a 30 day content plan, and the first posts shot on site.
Web FixA broken site repaired or a landing page built, ready for inquiries by the end of the day.

1. The fixes

On site at the client's door, or as online requests worked from the truck.

2. The show

YouTube and social streaming: every fix day is an episode (only with the client's written yes).

3. Sponsors and ads

The truck, the show and the kit carry partner brands that pay to ride along.

Page04

Brand persona

The Pit Crew

A racing pit crew does not explain the engine. It fixes the car in front of you, fast, and sends you back out.

PersonOwners and marketing managers of small and mid-size companies in Riyadh, then the rest of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA), who know their brand, social media or website is not working.
Pain"Agencies take six weeks and twenty emails, and we still don't get what we asked for." "Our Instagram looks like five different companies."
PromiseWe park at your door, fix it with you in one working day, and you watch every step.
Magician
60
Explorer
40

The Magician turns a broken brand around in a day. The Explorer leaves the office and drives to you.

Five traits, and what each one does to the design

FastOne motion curve, 240 and 480 milliseconds. Headlines of eight words or fewer.
PresentReal photos of the truck, the team and the client's own place, never stock. The orange dot means "here".
PreciseSquared type that echoes the logo letters; every number in a monospaced face; an 8 pixel grid.
BoldAsphalt black ground, white letters, and one orange moment per frame.
OpenBefore and after layouts, real screens, times and prices shown up front.

On a bad day

Magician gone wrong: "AI magic" hype with no time or number. Explorer gone wrong: a road show of driving footage with nothing delivered. The catch for both: every claim carries a time, a price or a result.

Test line: Would the Pit Crew say this?

Page05

Tone of voice

Say the fix.
Then the time.

Six principles

  • Say the fix, not the feature. "Your logo, cleaned up today", not "advanced AI design tools".
  • Time and price up front. Every offer names the day and the cost.
  • Short sentences. One idea each. Eight words in a headline at most.
  • Show, never promise. A before and after beats an adjective.
  • Plain words about AI. Say what it did, not what it is.
  • Saudi where we talk, formal where we sign. Saudi Arabic for social, streams, ads, the truck and chat; formal Arabic for quotes, invoices and contracts. First names only once the client uses ours.
FormalFriendly
SeriousPlayful
TechnicalPlain
ReservedEnthusiastic
We sayWe don't say
We'll park outside at 9 and hand over by 5.Seamless end-to-end creative solutions.
Your new logo files, ready today.A revolutionary AI-powered rebrand.
Here is the before. Here is the after.Trust the process.
We used AI to draft 40 layouts; you picked 3.Our AI magic does it all.
That is outside today's fix. Here is how we'd do it.Unfortunately we cannot accommodate that.

Words we use

fixtodayat your doorbefore and afterready bywe'll show youone day

Words we avoid

revolutionarycutting-edgegame-changerdisruptsynergyleveragemagicAI-powered

Writing rules: headlines up to eight words; numbers as digits (3 fixes, 9:00, 6,000 Saudi riyals (SAR)); every abbreviation spelled out the first time; no em dashes; one emoji per post at most, never in documents.

Voice in action

Ten moments

What we do, what we say, what we never say. Arabic lines are in Saudi Arabic, drafts until a Saudi copywriter signs them off.

1. A first message comes in

Do

Answer within the hour, name the fix and a date.

Say
Thanks for reaching out. Which one hurts most: brand, social or website? We can be at your door on Sunday.حيّاك الله وشكراً على تواصلك. وش أكثر شي يحتاج تصليح: الهوية، السوشال ميديا، ولا الموقع؟ نقدر نجيك يوم الأحد.
Never: "Please fill in our 20 question brief."

2. Confirming the booking

Do

Send time, parking need and what to prepare.

Say
Booked: Sunday, 9:00 to 17:00. We need one parking spot and your logo files if you have them.تم الحجز: الأحد من 9:00 إلى 17:00. نحتاج موقف واحد، وملفات شعارك لو عندك.
Never: a confirmation with no time on it.

3. Parking at their door

Do

Message on arrival; invite them in to see the studio.

Say
We're outside. Come and see the studio, coffee's on.وصلنا عند بابك. تفضّل شوف الاستوديو، والقهوة جاهزة.
Never: start work before the owner has seen the plan.

4. "Can AI really do this?"

Do

Show a real draft on the screen in minutes.

Say
Let's try it now. Give me ten minutes and pick the one you like.خلنا نجرّب الحين. عطني عشر دقايق واختار اللي يعجبك.
Never: a lecture on how the model works.

5. The handover

Do

Before and after on the big screen, files sent before we drive off.

Say
Here's where you started this morning. Here's where you are now. Everything is in your inbox.هذا اللي بدأنا فيه الصبح، وهذا وين وصلنا الحين. كل الملفات في إيميلك.
Never: "We'll send the files next week."

6. A request outside the three fixes

Do

Say no to today, yes to a plan.

Say
That's bigger than one day. We'll quote it as its own job by tomorrow.هذا أكبر من يوم واحد. بنرسل لك عرض سعر مستقل بكرة.
Never: squeeze it in and deliver half.

7. Running late

Do

Tell them before the time, with a new time.

Say
Traffic on King Fahd Road. We'll be there at 9:25, and we'll still hand over by 17:00.زحمة على طريق الملك فهد. بنوصل 9:25، والتسليم على موعده 17:00.
Never: arrive late and say nothing.

8. We made a mistake

Do

Own it, fix it, say when.

Say
The contact form on your site was broken by our update. It's fixed as of 14:10. Sorry.نموذج التواصل في موقعك تعطّل بسبب تحديثنا. تصلّح الساعة 14:10. نعتذر منك.
Never: "There was a technical issue."

9. Filming at a client's place

Do

Ask in writing before any camera turns on; blur screens.

Say
May we film today for our show? You see the cut before it goes out, and you can say no.تسمح لنا نصوّر اليوم لبرنامجنا؟ بتشوف المقطع قبل ننشره، ولك الحق ترفض.
Never: post a client's office, staff or screen without a written yes.

10. A sponsor asks to ride along

Do

Send the sponsor kit: where the brand shows, for how long, what it costs.

Say
Your brand on the truck and in 4 episodes a month. Here are the spots and the price.علامتك على الشاحنة وفي 4 حلقات بالشهر. هذي الأماكن والسعر.
Never: promise views we cannot show.

Page08

Construction

Measured by the dot

The orange dot is the unit, x. The clear space around the logo is 2x on every side.

The A

A cut by the road. Its peak is rounded; its feet are square.

The road

The thin cut in the A. It runs straight into the ring around the dot.

The dot

Signal orange, set in a ring cut into the I. Diameter 18.36 points in the master file: the unit x.

TRUCK

Custom squared letters, cap height half the I. Never retyped in a font.

Smallest sizes

Horizontal · 24 px screen · 8 mm print
Stacked · 48 px · 16 mm
Mark · 20 px · 6 mm

Below these sizes the road closes up and the dot turns into a speck. Embroidery and laser cut: stacked logo, 30 mm tall at least.

AI Truck brand systemv1 proposal. October 2026
Page09

Logo rules

Please don't

Recolour the letters

The letters are white or Asphalt. Orange belongs to the dot.

Stretch or squash

Scale with the corner handle, always in proportion.

Rotate or tilt

The logo always sits level, even on a moving vehicle graphic.

Add effects

No glow, shadow, outline, gradient or chrome. The van's light strips do the glowing.

AI TRUCK

Retype the name

Never set the logo in a font. Use the files.

White letters on orange

White on Signal is 3.05:1 and fails. On orange the letters are Asphalt.

Busy photo, no scrim

Over a photo, put a Deep scrim of 55% or more behind the logo.

Move or grow the dot

The dot stays in its ring at its size. It is the stop, not a sticker.

Page10

The motif

The Stop

A line that ends in an orange dot. The road that reaches your door, and the trace that reaches a node.

1. In the logo

The road cut through the A runs into the ring around the dot.

2. Lifted out

Line 1 unit thick, a gap of 1 unit, a dot 3 units across. The line can be any length; the gap and dot never change.

3. On the road

The orange stripe under the logo on the van is the Stop, with its dot at the front of the vehicle.

Six uses, and nothing else

1. Divider and footer rule

The rule at the foot of every page and slide.

  • Brand Fix
  • Social Fix
  • Web Fix
2. List bullet

A short line and a dot, in place of a round bullet.

9:00Park
10:00Diagnose
13:00Build
17:00Hand over
3. Route and progress

The fix day, a booking's status, a project timeline. Done stops are orange.

Ready by 5
4. The full stop

An orange full stop on the one headline that matters. Once per frame.

Today: Olaya, Riyadh
5. Where the truck is

Locations, map pins and the "today" post.

6. The transition

The dot grows to fill the frame and opens on the next scene (page 19).

Right to left: the line runs in the reading direction and the dot sits at the end of it, so in Arabic layouts the dot is on the left. On the truck: the dot always sits at the front of the vehicle, on both sides. There is never a second motif.

The colour system

Every pair, measured

Body text needs 4.5:1, large text (24 px, or 19 px bold) needs 3:1. Ratios computed with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 formula.

The orange in use today

The van mockups are AI renders, and each one drew the orange differently. The approved hex wins everywhere, including the wrap.

#FC5C18Concept board
#FC5000Rear view
#E85000Top view
#F26A2EWins

One orange text form per background

Ready by 5Signal on Asphalt · 5.34:1
Ready by 5Signal Ink on White · 5.05:1
Book a dayAsphalt on Signal · 5.34:1

Signal itself on White is 3.05:1 and on Chalk 2.76:1, so it never carries text on light; it may still fill a shape there (a dot, a button, a bar). White on Signal is 3.05:1: large text at most, and never on buttons.

Typography

Squared, like
the letters.

Three free families, each with one job. All from Google Fonts under the Open Font License, so there is nothing to buy and nothing to swap in Canva or Google Slides.

Headlines and body · Latin
Saira ExtraBold
Saira Regular for reading.

Squared curves and flat terminals, built like the TRUCK letters, without copying them. 800 headlines, 600 sub heads, 400 body, 300 large leads.

Arabic
إبداع ما يوقف
نصلّح هويتك في يوم واحد، عند بابك.

Changa: a squared Arabic that sits beside Saira. 700 headlines, 400 body. No letter spacing, no italics, line height 1.7 or more, first position on the right.

Numbers and data
1,386,000 SAR
09:00 · 21 days · 11 months

IBM Plex Mono for every number: equal-width digits, Western numerals, left to right even inside Arabic.

The letters inside the logo stay inside the logo. Headlines are never set in a font that imitates it, and the logo is never retyped.

Logo motion

Arrive. Park.
Open the door.

One curve

cubic-bezier(.3, .7, .2, 1). Fast start, soft stop, like a van parking.

Two speeds

240 ms for interface, 480 ms for scenes. A logo sting never passes 2.4 s.

No bounce, no spin

Things slide and land. The dot never pulses for attention.

The dot lands last

In every sting the orange dot is the final beat.

1. Arrive

The A and I rise, TRUCK follows letter by letter, the dot drops into its ring. Video intros and the website's first load.

2. Drive in

The logo drives in from the start side and parks; the road draws under it and the dot lights up. Reel and story openers.

Before
After

The dot grows to fill the frame and opens on the next scene. The only transition: before to after, slide to slide.

Laws and matrix

Eight laws

What holds when everything else bends.

Signal acts once per frame

One orange moment: the dot, the button or the key word. A second highlight cancels the first.

Orange text has a form per background

Signal on dark, Signal Ink on light, and Asphalt on an orange fill. Never white text on orange.

The background follows the audience

Asphalt for the public: truck, social, show, website, decks. Chalk for what a client reads or signs: quotes, invoices, reports.

Group with space first

Then a shared colour, then a shared background. A border only when all three fail.

Every number has a source

In IBM Plex Mono, Western digits, left to right. Projected figures say "projected" and never look like results.

Arabic is a first language

Saudi where we talk, formal where we sign. Changa, no letter spacing, no italics, first position on the right, the Stop mirrored.

One curve, the dot lands last

cubic-bezier(.3, .7, .2, 1) at 240 or 480 ms. Nothing bounces, spins or pulses.

No camera without a yes

Never film, stream or post a client, their staff or their screens without a written yes. "LIVE" and "REC" appear only when true; client screens are blurred by default.

Design tokens

The system as code

Every value in this book as CSS (the website's style code). The website in step 3 reads from this file.

/* AI Truck design tokens, v1 (proposal, 2026-10-13).
   Sources: Asphalt #231F20 read off the supplied logo PDF (every path fill, 18 of 18).
            Signal #F26A2E given by Amer on 2026-10-13 (the PDF is one colour).
   Every other colour is built from those two in OKLCH and measured (WCAG 2.1 ratios in comments).
   Laws: see README.md. Signal acts; Asphalt grounds; Chalk and White breathe. */

:root {
  /* ---- core ---- */
  --at-signal:      #F26A2E; /* ACTS: the dot, the one action, the one highlight. 5.34:1 on Asphalt, 4.64:1 on Raised */
  --at-asphalt:     #231F20; /* GROUNDS: the van, dark backgrounds, text on light. 16.30:1 on White */
  --at-white:       #FFFFFF; /* SPEAKS: logo letters and text on dark */
  --at-chalk:       #F5F3F1; /* BREATHES: light backgrounds for documents. Asphalt on Chalk 14.73:1 */

  /* ---- support, built by construction ---- */
  --at-raised:      #2E2A2B; /* cards on Asphalt */
  --at-deep:        #161314; /* the deepest layer: photo scrims, page behind sheets */
  --at-steel:       #A29D9E; /* secondary text on dark: 5.30:1 on Raised, 6.10:1 on Asphalt */
  --at-slate:       #6C6769; /* secondary text on light: 5.02:1 on Chalk, 5.55:1 on White */
  --at-signal-ink:  #C64100; /* orange TEXT on light: 4.56:1 on Chalk, 5.05:1 on White */
  --at-on-signal:   #231F20; /* text on an orange fill is always Asphalt: 5.34:1. White fails (3.05:1) */

  /* ---- states: report a state only, always with an icon and words ---- */
  --at-go:          #00813F; --at-go-dk:   #2BA661; /* done, live, paid */
  --at-wait:        #1C70C7; --at-wait-dk: #4695F0; /* booked, on the way, in progress */
  --at-stop:        #D3134F; --at-stop-dk: #FF5277; /* error, cancelled. Hue 13, kept 29 degrees from Signal (42) */

  /* ---- scales (OKLCH lightness walk, brand hue held) ---- */
  --at-signal-50:#FFF2EC; --at-signal-100:#FFE0D3; --at-signal-200:#FFC0A8; --at-signal-300:#FB9B76; --at-signal-400:#F67D4D;
  --at-signal-500:#F26A2E; --at-signal-600:#C75016; --at-signal-700:#A23A00; --at-signal-800:#7E2500; --at-signal-900:#5B1200;
  --at-asphalt-50:#F9F3F5; --at-asphalt-100:#E8E3E4; --at-asphalt-200:#D2CCCD; --at-asphalt-300:#B5AFB1; --at-asphalt-400:#969192;
  --at-asphalt-500:#787374; --at-asphalt-600:#5B5758; --at-asphalt-700:#403C3D; --at-asphalt-800:#312C2E; --at-asphalt-900:#231F20;

  /* ---- type ---- */
  --at-font-display: "Saira", "Arial Narrow", Arial, sans-serif;      /* 800 headlines, 600 sub heads */
  --at-font-body:    "Saira", Arial, sans-serif;                      /* 400 body, 300 large leads */
  --at-font-arabic:  "Changa", Tahoma, sans-serif;                    /* 700 headlines, 400 body. No tracking, no italics */
  --at-font-data:    "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace; /* every number: tabular, Western digits, left to right */

  /* ---- shape, space, motion ---- */
  --at-radius:      6px;     /* small, squared corners like the logo's letters */
  --at-radius-lg:   14px;
  --at-space:       8px;     /* base step; use 8, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96 */
  --at-ease:        cubic-bezier(.3,.7,.2,1); /* the one curve. Nothing bounces or spins */
  --at-fast:        240ms;
  --at-slow:        480ms;

  /* ---- the motif: the Stop (a line that ends in a ringed dot) ---- */
  --at-stop-line:   2px;     /* line weight at 16px dot; scales 1 : 8 with the dot */
  --at-stop-dot:    16px;
}

/* ---- themes: the background follows the audience ---- */
.at-dark  { --bg: var(--at-asphalt); --fg: var(--at-white);   --fg2: var(--at-steel); --card: var(--at-raised);
            --accent-text: var(--at-signal);     --line: rgba(162,157,158,.28); background: var(--bg); color: var(--fg); }
.at-light { --bg: var(--at-chalk);   --fg: var(--at-asphalt); --fg2: var(--at-slate); --card: var(--at-white);
            --accent-text: var(--at-signal-ink); --line: rgba(35,31,32,.14);    background: var(--bg); color: var(--fg); }

/* ---- utilities ---- */
.at-num     { font-family: var(--at-font-data); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; direction: ltr; unicode-bidi: isolate; }
.at-eyebrow { font-family: var(--at-font-display); font-weight: 600; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: .14em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--accent-text); }
.at-eyebrow:lang(ar) { font-family: var(--at-font-arabic); letter-spacing: 0; text-transform: none; font-weight: 700; }
.at-source  { font-family: var(--at-font-data); font-size: 12px; color: var(--fg2); }
.at-btn     { font-family: var(--at-font-display); font-weight: 700; background: var(--at-signal); color: var(--at-on-signal);
              border: 0; border-radius: var(--at-radius); padding: 12px 22px; transition: transform var(--at-fast) var(--at-ease); }

01Signal orange #F26A2E everywhere, over the mockups' redder oranges.

08The Stop as the one motif, with the dot at the front of the truck.
09The name stays in Latin letters inside Arabic text; no Arabic logo for now.
10Law 8: no camera without the client's written yes; client screens blurred.
11Saudi Arabic lines reviewed by a Saudi copywriter before anything goes out.
12Before wrapping: vinyl proof of Signal at dusk, gloss or matte, and the Riyadh vehicle advertising rules.
